Header.title: I traded the microscope for code.
Header.intro: I’m {name}. I studied biotechnology engineering and worked in a neurobiology lab before moving into software. Today I build the quote, payment and after-sales flows for Seguros Falabella with React, Next.js, NestJS and Strapi, and AI is part of my everyday work.
Header.channels: Cultured neuron, three channels. Switch one off to see each layer.

About.title: From the lab to web development.
About.lab: I studied biotechnology engineering and spent three years in a neurobiology lab doing statistics, data analysis and bioinformatics. That’s where I learned not to trust a result until I can reproduce it.
About.code: In 2016 I started building online stores, and since 2022 I’ve worked as a full stack developer. The lab habit came with me: I test, measure and review before I call anything done.

Projects.title: Five stages, <hl>one customer</hl>.
Projects.body: Five applications that, in order, cover what a person does with their insurance: get a quote, buy it, pay for it, sign in to their account and handle requests.

Architecture.title: Under the hood, <hl>one architecture</hl>.
Architecture.body: The five applications share the same layers: a frontend in Next.js or React, NestJS services with hexagonal architecture, content in Strapi and data in MongoDB. Each layer has a single job, so a frontend can be migrated or an integration swapped without touching the business rules.
Architecture.rule: Dependencies point inward: the domain knows nothing about NestJS, MongoDB or HTTP.
Architecture.skill: It’s the same pattern I taught the agent in a skill

Ai.title: I use AI every day. And I <hl>review everything</hl> it writes.
Ai.body: I come from analyzing data in a lab, so I treat a language model like any other instrument: fast and useful, but I don’t trust it until I’ve checked.

Skills.title: What I work with.
Skills.body: Each well is a technology I use, sorted by channel: frontend, backend, AI, data and tools.

Contact.title: Let’s talk.
Contact.body: Looking for a full stack developer for your team? Email me: it’s the most direct way to reach me, and I reply quickly.

System.metaDescription: The tokens, type and components behind this portfolio: one set of tokens for two looks, fluorescence and brightfield.
System.title: Design system
System.intro: This portfolio uses one set of tokens for two looks: fluorescence (light adding up on black) and brightfield (stains absorbing light on white). This page reads the values straight from the CSS at build time, so it always matches what you see.
System.tokensBody: Every color is named for its job, not its hue. Brightfield adds no styles of its own: it redefines these same tokens.
System.contrastNote: The number next to each color is its contrast: body text on top of it for surfaces, and the color on the page background for the rest.
System.channelsTitle: One channel per part of the work
System.channelsBody: As in a fluorescence image, each channel shows a single structure. Here each one marks a part of my work, and that meaning holds across the site: the neuron, the stack columns, the architecture layers and the logo. Section colors are separate, so emphasis is never mistaken for a channel.
System.typeBody: Archivo, variable, using its width axis: headings run wide and body text stays normal. Martian Mono for labels and data, like an instrument readout.
System.sampleText: I build the quote, payment and after-sales flows of Seguros Falabella with React, Next.js, NestJS and Strapi.
System.logoBody: My initials as a closing tag, with one channel in each symbol.

principles.tokens: Components use no fixed colors: everything goes through the tokens, and switching modes only redefines them. The only exceptions are the swatches on this page and the share image, which can't read CSS.
principles.contrast: Body text, secondary text and the six section colors all clear 4.5:1 (WCAG AA) in both modes. The lowest is {min}:1.
principles.blend: In fluorescence the channels add up (plus-lighter), like light; in brightfield they multiply, like stains.
principles.hover: Each control answers the pointer with a different microscope technique: the primary button splits its three channels, the secondary one opens the field diaphragm, links underline one channel at a time, like a confocal scan, and arrows move the stage to the next field. Keyboard focus gets the same answer.
principles.motion: With reduced motion nothing animates: not the sections coming into focus, not the screenshot cycle.
principles.focus: Keyboard focus is always visible, and the smallest controls (the screenshots, the carousel scale and the channels) take a tap across about 44 px.
